rationale: Economically coherent and the continuous working-capital-stress conditioner is a legitimate change, but ebitda/at is essentially the archive's oibdp/at profitability core re-scaled by a new rank, making this a mild conditioner swap on an already-tested profitability×balance-sheet-stress template rather than a substantively new mechanism.

This is a near-rediscovery of the archive's "Debt-Loaded Operating Profitability" (same IND_ADJ operating profitability core, same total-debt-to-assets conditioner) with only cosmetic changes — subtracting xint and swapping RANK-of-sum for SUMRANK — and the interest subtraction also partially collapses the interaction into the conditioner itself.

The change-in-gross-profitability core is genuinely distinct from the archive's level-profitability and operating-margin-change signals, and total-liability leverage is a reasonable conditioner, though the underlying "profitability improvement is worth more under distress" mechanism has already produced weak evidence in this archive (Retained-Deficit Margin Repair) so the prior is not encouraging.

The most substantively different proposal here — a cost-efficiency-deterioration core rather than a profitability level, interacted with working-capital stress — with a hypothesis whose expected negative sign matches the expression's natural direction (the rank conditioner is non-negative, so sign is driven by ΔSG&A/revenue as intended).

The conditioner is internally inconsistent with the stated cross-theme intent because txt/at is mechanically a profitability proxy, so half the SUMRANK turns the signal into a convex transform of operating profitability itself rather than an independent distress-credibility conditioner.

Accounting error plus rediscovery: oibdp already expenses R&D, so subtracting xrd double-counts it and invalidates the "profits after funding innovation" story, and the remainder is the archive's Debt-Loaded Operating Profitability with the identical total-debt conditioner.
